choices.reason: No rule yields a unique candidate: creative performance is named primary, but the abstract gives AUT and PIT equal emphasis and neither task is designated the main one. Both tasks use the same randomized arms, were presented in random order, and lack qualifying participant-level SDs or data_stats; the remaining rules therefore do not resolve the task tie.
choices.locator: PDF p. 9, section 2.2 (primary outcome); p. 2, Abstract (both tasks); p. 10, section 2.3 (random task order); pp. 17 and 21-22, Tables 2 and 4 and role comparisons (statistics).
choices.quote: Creative performance served as the primary outcome variable, including idea novelty, usefulness, flexibility, and fluency. [...] In both AUT and PIT tasks, human−AI collaboration showed significantly higher idea novelty and more frequent perspective-taking than human−human collaboration.
